title: Extending a list prefix past a dropped head
statement: Let $l$ be a list over a type $\alpha$, let $n$ be a natural number, and suppose that dropping the first $n$ entries of $l$ leaves a nonempty list whose head is $a$ (so that $l$ has more than $n$ entries and its $(n+1)$-st entry is $a$). Then the prefix consisting of the first $n+1$ entries of $l$ equals the prefix consisting of the first $n$ entries with $a$ appended: taking $n+1$ entries of $l$ gives (taking $n$ entries of $l$) followed by $[a]$.
hypotheses_covered: dropping the first n entries of l yields a list with head a (i.e. l.drop n = a :: rest)
